# Engine snapshots that were ALREADY PUBLIC on github.com/VortXTV/VortX before the guard
# existed. This is a record of an incident, not permission for a new one.
#
# WHAT THESE ARE
# Each line is the git tree OID of a vortx-core/ snapshot that is reachable from a branch
# or tag on the public repository. They are listed by snapshot rather than by commit
# because 1139 commits carry only these 100 distinct trees: the tree is the content that
# leaked, the commit is just one of many places it appears.
#
# WHY THE FILE EXISTS
# .github/workflows/engine-leak-guard.yml sweeps every ref for engine material. Without
# this list it would fail on day one and keep failing, because the engine is reachable
# from 913 commits in the default branch's own history. A check that is permanently red
# gets muted, and a muted check is not a check. Baselining what already leaked is what
# lets the sweep report the only thing it can still act on: something NEW leaking.
#
# WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
# It does not unpublish anything, and the pre-push hook deliberately ignores it. The hook
# blocks engine material reaching a public remote whether or not that exact snapshot has
# leaked before. Only the after-the-fact CI sweep consults this list.
#
# THIS FILE SHOULD SHRINK, NEVER GROW.
# A new entry means something leaked. Adding one is an incident record and needs the same
# scrutiny as the leak itself. Removing one means history was genuinely rewritten.
#
# Regenerate the current exposure (does not write this file):
#   git ls-remote --heads --tags <public-remote> | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u \
#     | git rev-list --stdin | sort -u \
#     | scripts/scan-proprietary-engine.sh paths - | awk '{print $4}' | sort -u
#
# Captured 2026-07-25 from 294 live public refs, 2769 reachable commits, 1139 carrying an engine tree.
